# Why Do We Need RNNs?

## Feedforward Networks Assume Independence

For MLPs:

$$
x_i \perp x_j
$$

But many datasets are sequential:

- Text
- Speech
- Financial time-series
- Biological sequences
- Sensor signals

---

## Sequential Dependency

Language modeling:

$$
P(w_t | w_{t-1}, w_{t-2}, ..., w_1)
$$

The past matters.

---

## Applications

- Language modeling
- Machine translation
- Speech recognition
- Time-series forecasting
- Genomics
- Video processing

# The Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)

## Core Recurrence

$$
h_t = \sigma(W_h h_{t-1} + W_x x_t + b)
$$

$$
y_t = W_y h_t
$$

Same weights reused across time.

---

## Unrolled Through Time

![Unrolled RNN](/images/rnn_unrolled.png)

---

## TensorFlow: Simple RNN

```{python}
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers

model = keras.Sequential([
    layers.SimpleRNN(64, return_sequences=True),
    layers.SimpleRNN(32),
    layers.Dense(1)
])

model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="mse")
model.summary()
```

---

## Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)

Training objective:

$$
\frac{\partial L}{\partial W} =\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{\partial L}{\partial h_t}\frac{\partial h_t}{\partial W}
$$

But:

$$
\frac{\partial h_t}{\partial h_{t-k}}=\prod_{i=t-k+1}^{t}\frac{\partial h_i}{\partial h_{i-1}}
$$

Repeated matrix multiplication → instability.

# Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)

## Key Idea

![LSTM Cell](/images/lstm_architecture.png)

:::{.callout-note}
Allow constant error flow through a memory cell.
:::

---


## LSTM Equations

**Forget gate:**

$$
f_t = \sigma(W_f [h_{t-1}, x_t])
$$

**Input gate:**

$$
i_t = \sigma(W_i [h_{t-1}, x_t])
$$

**Cell update:**

$$
c_t = f_t \odot c_{t-1} + i_t \odot \tilde{c}_t
$$

**Output:**

$$
h_t = o_t \odot \tanh(c_t)
$$

---

## Why LSTM Works

If:

$$
f_t \approx 1
$$

Then:

$$
\frac{\partial c_t}{\partial c_{t-1}} \approx 1
$$

>Gradient preserved.

---

## Tensorflow: LSTM

```{python}
model = keras.Sequential([
    layers.LSTM(64, return_sequences=True),
    layers.LSTM(32),
    layers.Dense(1)
])

model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="mse")
```

# Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)

## GRU Architecture

>Simpler alternative to LSTM.

![GRU Cell](/images/gru_architecture.png)

## GRU Equations

**Update gate:**

$$
z_t = \sigma(W_z [h_{t-1}, x_t])
$$

**Reset gate:**

$$
r_t = \sigma(W_r [h_{t-1}, x_t])
$$

**Final Update:**

$$
h_t = (1 - z_t) \odot h_{t-1} + z_t \odot \widetilde{h}_t
$$

---

## Tensorflow: GRU

```{python}
model = keras.Sequential([
    layers.GRU(64, return_sequences=True),
    layers.GRU(32),
    layers.Dense(1)
])
```

# Regularization in RNNs

## Recurrent Dropout

Standard dropout disrupts temporal memory.

**Recurrent dropout:**

- Applied on recurrent connections
- Same mask across timesteps

---

## TensorFlow: Recurrent Dropout

```{python}
model = keras.Sequential([
    layers.LSTM(
        64,
        return_sequences=True,
        dropout=0.2,
        recurrent_dropout=0.2
    ),
    layers.LSTM(32),
    layers.Dense(1)
])
```

---

## Gradient Clipping

$$
\nabla_\theta L \leftarrow \frac{\nabla_\theta L}{\max(1, \frac{||\nabla_\theta L||}{\text{clipnorm}})}
$$

Prevent exploding gradients:

```{python}
optimizer = tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
    learning_rate=0.001,
    clipnorm=1.0
)
```

# Final Notes

## Model Comparison

| Model | Long Dependencies | Complexity | Speed  |
| ----- | ----------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| RNN   | Poor              | Low        | Fast   |
| LSTM  | Excellent         | High       | Slower |
| GRU   | Very Good         | Medium     | Faster |

## Limitations of RNNs

- Sequential computation
- Hard to parallelize
- Long sequences still challenging
- Transformers dominate NLP
